message.content: Triage on the known force-limit failure — shrinking it to the minimal case and pinning the cause.
I've pinpointed the velocity spike triggering the violation — now testing a counterfactual tweak to confirm the mechanism.

function.arguments: {"scenario_id":"s7af96630b1","rule":"controller_force_limit","explanation":"Controller force violates fmax after a body-body collision. At step 28 bodies 0 and 1 are in near-contact (gap ~0.005) with low controller force. The collision impulse at step 29 gives body 0 a large velocity jump (speed 2.9 -> 10.27, vy -2.14 -> +8.42). The velocity-error controller computes force = kp * (v_desired - v_actual) which scales with the post-impact velocity error (kp 26.76) to ~487 N, exceeding fmax 72.67 without effective clamping. Lowering kp to 5 keeps the same collision but keeps the computed force within/at the limit (clamped), proving the gain vs limit interaction is the cause.","citations":[{"body":0,"claim":"controller force well within limit just before collision, bodies in near contact","field":"speed","step":28,"value":2.9080937464537344},{"body":0,"claim":"first violation: controller force exceeds fmax 72.67","field":"speed","step":29,"value":10.27091271082136}],"counterfactual":{"scenario_id":"s00d2be2f8a","change":"reduced kp from 26.765 to 5.0 (single field) – same collision occurs but kp*error now stays within/clamped to fmax, so no violation"}}
